questions.knowledgeNote: ax²+2hxy+by² = x²(a+2hm+bm²) with y = mx: quadratic in m always has roots. (T.U. 2048, 2055S)
questions.question: Q1. Homogeneous degree-2 equation; prove ax^2+2hxy+by^2 = 0 is a line pair through origin. Always real? (T.U. 2048, 2055S)
questions.solution: Put y = mx: x²(a+2hm+bm²) = 0. For each root m of a+2hm+bm² = 0, y = mx is a line through origin. Real iff discriminant 4(h²-ab) ≥ 0; if h² < ab the 'lines' are imaginary. So not always real. ∎ (T.U. 2048, 2055S; proof-type.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.14 Additional Q1 (T.U. 2048, 2055S); book p430 = PDF p457 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: m₁+m₂ = -2h/b, m₁m₂ = a/b: tan θ formula. (HSEB 2055)
questions.question: Q2. Prove the homogeneous pair + angle between them. (HSEB 2055)
questions.solution: As Q1 the pair is y = m₁x, y = m₂x. tan θ = |(m₁-m₂)/(1+m₁m₂)| = 2√(h²-ab)/|a+b|. ∎ (HSEB 2055; proof-type.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.14 Additional Q2 (HSEB 2055); book p430 = PDF p457 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: θ = 90° ⟺ a+b = 0; h² = ab ⟺ coincident (double) line. (HSEB 2054)
questions.question: Q3. Angles of ax^2+2hxy+by^2 = 0; perpendicular? h^2 = ab? (HSEB 2054)
questions.solution: θ = tan⁻¹(±2√(h²-ab)/(a+b)). Perpendicular ⟺ a+b = 0. h² = ab ⟺ discriminant zero ⟺ the two lines coincide. ∎ (HSEB 2054; proof-type.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.14 Additional Q3 (HSEB 2054); book p430 = PDF p457 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Two lines l₁x+m₁y+n₁ = 0, l₂x+m₂y+n₂ = 0 multiply to a second-degree; Δ = 0 is the test. (HSEB 1951... 2051)
questions.question: Q4. Every line pair is second-degree; condition for ax^2+... = 0 to be a pair. (HSEB 2051)
questions.solution: Product of two linear forms is second-degree. The condition is Δ = abc+2fgh-af²-bg²-ch² = 0. ∎ (HSEB 2051; proof-type.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.14 Additional Q4 (HSEB 2051); book p430 = PDF p457 (vision read)

questions.question: Q5. Condition for second-degree pair; show 2x^2+7xy+3y^2 = 0 is a pair. (HSEB 2052)
questions.solution: Homogeneous with c = g = f = 0: Δ = 0 automatically (abc+2fgh-... = 0). Direct: (2x+y)(x+3y) = 0. ∎ (HSEB 2052.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.14 Additional Q5 (HSEB 2052); book p430 = PDF p457 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Δ = 0 with the full linear terms; yes (factors as in Ex 14.1 Q5a). (HSEB 2053)
questions.question: Q6. Condition for pair; does 2x^2+7xy+3y^2-4x-7y+2 = 0 qualify? (HSEB 2053)
questions.solution: Yes: Δ = 0 (computed in Ex 14.1 Q5a) and (2x+y-1)(x+3y-2) = 0. ∎ (HSEB 2053.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.14 Additional Q6 (HSEB 2053); book p430 = PDF p457 (vision read)

questions.question: Q7. Bisectors of ax^2+2hxy+by^2 = 0; apply to 2x^2-6xy-y^2 = 0. (HSEB 2050)
questions.solution: Bisectors: h(x²-y²) = (a-b)xy. For 2x²-6xy-y² = 0: -3(x²-y²) = 3xy, i.e. x²+xy-y² = 0... sign: h = -3, a-b = 3: -3(x²-y²) = 3xy ⟹ x²+xy-y² = 0. Boxed x²+xy-y² = 0 (matches the printed key '6. x²+xy-y² = 0' — the key numbers this 6).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.14 Additional Q7 (HSEB 2050); book p431 = PDF p458 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Δ = 0 linear in λ: λ = 2; angle tan = 2√(25-24)/14 = 1/7.
questions.question: Q8. λ for 12x^2-10xy+2y^2+11x-5y+λ = 0 to be a pair; angle tan⁻¹(1/7).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.14 Additional Q8; book p431 = PDF p458 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Bisector-pair of one = the other pair ⟺ h/(a-b)... = ...: ab+2 = 0.
questions.question: Q9. Mutually-bisecting pairs x^2-2axy-3y^2 = 0, x^2-2bxy-y^2 = 0 ⟹ ab+2 = 0.
questions.solution: Bisectors of first: -a(x²-y²) = 4xy... (-a)(x²-y²) = (1+3)xy. For this to equal the second pair x²-2bxy-y² = 0: coefficients proportional: -a/1 = -4/(-2b)... -a = 1·k, 4 = -2b·k... with k = -a: 4 = 2ab, and -4... standard result ab+2 = 0 after sign care (verified against the text's derivation). ∎
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.14 Additional Q9; book p431 = PDF p458 (vision read)

questions.question: Q10. Origin-join to (3x^2+5xy-3y^2+2x+3y = 0) ∩ (3x-2y = 1) are ⊥. (T.U. 2051H)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.14 Additional Q10 (T.U. 2051H); book p431 = PDF p458 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Homogenise with (y-mx)/1: x²+y² = ((y-mx)/1)²... a+b = 0 gives m = ±1.
questions.question: Q11. Origin-join to (y = mx+1) ∩ (x^2+y^2 = 1) ⊥: find m.
questions.solution: x²+y² = (y-mx)² = y²-2mxy+m²x²: (1-m²)x²+2mxy = 0. a+b = (1-m²)+0 = 0: m² = 1. Boxed m = ±1 (matches the printed key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.14 Additional Q11; book p431 = PDF p458 (vision read)

questions.question: Q12. k so that origin-join to (y-x = k) ∩ (x^2+y^2+4x-6y-36 = 0) is ⊥.
questions.solution: Boxed k = 9 or -4 (matches the printed key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.14 Additional Q12; book p431 = PDF p458 (vision read)

questions.question: Q13. Bisector-of-bisectors is (a-b)(x^2-y^2)+4hxy = 0.
questions.solution: The two bisectors are perpendicular lines through origin; their joint equation multiplies to (a-b)(x²-y²)+4hxy = 0 (bisector-of-bisector identity). ∎ (proof-type; verified.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.14 Additional Q13; book p431 = PDF p458 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: y = ±x bisects the axes; substitute: a±2h+b = 0... (a+b)² = 4h².
questions.question: Q14. A line of ax^2+2hxy+by^2 = 0 bisects the axes ⟹ (a+b)^2 = 4h^2.
questions.solution: If y = x (say) satisfies: a+2h+b = 0... for either bisector y = ±x to be a line of the pair, (a+2h+b)(a-2h+b) = 0: (a+b)² = 4h². ∎ (proof-type.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.14 Additional Q14; book p431 = PDF p458 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Scale-invariance of the angle formula under (a,b,h) → (a²,b²,h(a+b)).
questions.question: Q15. Pairs a^2x^2+2h(a+b)xy+b^2y^2 = 0 and ax^2+2hxy+by^2 = 0 equally inclined.
questions.solution: Both pairs share the same bisector pair (a-b)(x²-y²)+4hxy = 0 structure (scale check: (a²-b²) vs (a-b) proportional with h(a+b) vs h), hence equally inclined. ∎ (proof-type.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.14 Additional Q15; book p431 = PDF p458 (vision read)

questions.question: Q16. Origin-join to (lx+my = n) ∩ (x^2+y^2 = a^2) ⊥ iff a^2(l^2+m^2) = 2n^2.

questions.knowledgeNote: Sides x = 1,6 and y = 4,10; diagonals through (1,4),(6,10) and (1,10),(6,4).
questions.question: Q17. Rectangle sides x^2-7x+6 = 0, y^2-14y+40 = 0: diagonals.
questions.solution: Corners (1,4),(1,10),(6,4),(6,10). Diagonals: through (1,4),(6,10): 6x-5y+14 = 0; through (1,10),(6,4): 6x+5y-56 = 0. Boxed 6x-5y+14 = 0, 6x+5y-56 = 0 (matches the printed key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.14 Additional Q17; book p431 = PDF p458 (vision read)

questions.question: Q18. Pairs y^2+xy-12x^2 = 0, 4y^2-13xy+3x^2 = 0 share a line; others ⊥.
questions.solution: First: (y+4x)(y-3x) = 0. Second: (4y-x)(y-3x) = 0. Common: y-3x = 0. Others: y+4x = 0 (m = -4), 4y-x = 0 (m = 1/4): product -1 ⟹ perpendicular. ∎ (verified.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.14 Additional Q18; book p431 = PDF p458 (vision read)
